x: Eric Gebbett was the early pacemaker from Beale of Shaftsbury and at twelve miles he was passed by Haslam(T.V.H.) and Salvat(Finchley). Len Bishop, who had been content to hang back in the early stages, now began to move up and at sixteen miles passed Eric at great speed.

Hewson out---Rowe out---Salvat and Ranjit Bhatia out; what a start! and then Bruce Tulloh, after a tremendous fight, was also eliminated. But saddest of all we saw the slender, loping figure of Gordon Pirie----the only man to stop the incessant "RA!RA!RA!

Barry Sawyer came home on Stage 4 with an 8 second lead from Portsmouth(Salvat) and it seemed that our opponents would go on for ever changing places behind us while Belgrave, unostentatiously, held the van.

Barry Sawyer continued his good work of the previous weeks and closed to within 5 secs of Portsmouth's Salvat in taking us up to 2nd. John Thresher then produced a brilliant run to leave Hayden standing and record 3rd fastest time of the day---our deficit being turned into a 19 seconds lead.

John Moore set off on stage 2 (4½ miles) behind Salvat of Portsmouth and the Ryde runner. He soon passed the latter but could make no impression on the 'bearded wonder' who is a very seasoned campaigner and always a difficult opponent.
Tony Fairclough, not at his best, watched Tulloh disappear into the distance and Kerr lost further ground to Salvat, so Gerry North was faced with a deficit of 69 seconds on the final leg.
